In DSM‑5, Criteria A through C together specify the core requirements for diagnosing a personality disorder: Criterion A addresses the level of impairment in personality functioning, Criterion B covers the presence of pathological personality traits, and Criterion C requires that these impairments and traits be relatively inflexible and pervasive across a range of personal and social situations [Psichiatry_DSM-5_3555].
